meta.title: Reference alignment, WAB -> Wittgensteiniana (Pasin), draft v2
meta.status: draft: manual, semi-formal, revised on review
meta.revision_v2: v1 mapped Part -> Thesis (C2). Removed: the numbered TLP propositions are already linked instance-to-instance across both ontologies by the TractatusProposition bridge overlay (tractatus_alignment_layer.ttl, ~530 shared individuals), so a class-level Part -> Thesis mapping would duplicate the bridge. Part maps to Chapter (C2 in this version).
meta.revision_v3: Removed the redundant ex:Thesis normalization layer from wittgensteiniana_final.ttl: the original Pasin export types the proposition units schema:Chapter ONLY; ex:Thesis was added on the same individuals by build_wittgensteiniana_final.py, so the two classes were extensionally identical (526 = 526, no class counterpart differences). The units are schema:Chapter everywhere now; bridge extraction and retriever top_k were updated accordingly.
meta.grounding: class/property definitions and rdfs:comment content documented in the comment overlays (wab_tractatus_comments.ttl, wittgensteiniana_comments.ttl), plus instance-level samples from both datasets
meta.grading_note: class-level and property-level scores are graded separately; 'instances' lists grounding evidence

class_mappings.justification: WAB: a publication of a Wittgenstein primary source known as a work by Wittgenstein; single instance W-TLP = Tractatus logico-philosophicus. Wittgensteiniana: schema:Book is used only for the three published works (German original + Ogden 1922 + Pears/McGuinness 1961 editions).

In the original Wittgensteiniana export the proposition units are typed schema:Chapter (the only chapter-like class there; see meta.revision_v3). WAB Part instances (531) are labelled 'Tractatus logico-philosophicus (TLP, 1922 et 1933) <number>' (e.g. 'TLP 1.1') - individual numbered TLP remarks.

WAB Bemerkung (1616): a remark identified by a siglum - the material textual record of a remark in a Wittgenstein source. Wittgensteiniana TextFragment (1578): the symbolic contents of a text unit, in the export one fragment per proposition per edition/language (both double-typed schema:CreativeWork).

class_mappings.note: acceptable-but-discussed: both are generic 'textual resource' supertypes, but WAB's substructure (Werk/Bemerkung/Part/TS) has no direct counterpart downstream
class_mappings.justification: WAB WittgensteinSource is the generic superclass of Werk, Bemerkung, Part, TS; schema:CreativeWork is the generic superclass Book/text fragments under schema.org typing.

Both classes cover persons. WAB scholar:Person (21 instances): historical persons (Plato, Paul Wittgenstein, authors of external sources). Wittgensteiniana ex:Author (4): Wittgenstein + translators (Ogden, Pears, McGuinness), assigned as book authors. Authorship is a role of scholar:Person, so the match holds at class level.

property_mappings.justification: same URI tail, same compositional semantics (item part of item).
WAB hasPart = owl:inverseOf isPartOf (WAB ontology declares it); schema:isPartOf expressed in the same direction as WAB isPartOf.
both link a work to its author (range: person/author class).
both give the language of the content of a source/creative work.

both connect a text resource ('source mentions it') to the target resource; the exact domains/ranges differ (refersTo: source -> person/werk/bemerkung/external source; mentions: thesis -> defined term).

rejections.reason: a string-based match earlier suggested contains->mentions; but contains points from a WittgensteinSource to scholar:TextSubGenre (a genre!), which has no counterpart in Wittgensteiniana.
a string-based match earlier suggested isDateOf->isPartOf; isDateOf relates scholar:Date -> Bemerkung - temporal data has no counterpart.
estimated source dating constraints; schema:datePublished is a first-publication date, not an estimate band - rejected.
typed primary sources / manuscript items (W-Ts-202, 1619 instances); Wittgensteiniana's published-book types (Book) have no manuscript counterpart.
works by other authors (Frege, Paul Ernst etc.); Wittgensteiniana CreativeWork is used exclusively for text fragments in this dataset.
